successCriteria.description: The `findByLeaveType` SQL query includes `AND is_active = true` so that only active policies are returned. The WHERE clause must be `WHERE leave_type = $1 AND is_active = true`.
When the database returns a row with `is_active = false` for the requested leave type, `findByLeaveType` returns `null` (the inactive row is excluded by the query filter).
When both an active and an inactive row exist for the same leave type, `findByLeaveType` returns only the active policy (the inactive row is excluded by the query filter).
The existing unit test in `tests/unit/modules/policy/policy.repository.test.ts` for `findByLeaveType` is updated to assert the new SQL string containing `AND is_active = true`.

constraints: The `findByLeaveType` method signature on `IPolicyRepository` must NOT change — it still accepts `LeaveType` and returns `Promise<LeavePolicy | null>`. Only the SQL WHERE clause changes.
The `findAllActive` method must remain unchanged — it already filters by `is_active = true` and serves as the reference pattern for this change.
outOfScope: No changes to `findAllActive`, `findById`, `create`, or `update` methods — they already behave correctly.
No changes to the `LeavePolicy` model or `IPolicyRepository` interface signatures.

entityInvariants.invariant: Repository query methods that return a single policy by lookup criteria (`findByLeaveType`) must only return policies whose `isActive` is `true` — inactive policies are excluded at the query level, not filtered in application code.

interfaceConstraints.authRule: N/A — repository layer; no auth rule applies
interfaceConstraints.errorSemantics: Returns null when no active policy matches the leave type (including when only an inactive policy exists). No thrown errors for missing rows.

consistencyRequirements.requirement: The `findByLeaveType` SQL query must use the same `is_active = true` filter pattern already established by `findAllActive` in the same file.
